mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: microwave absorption enhancement of BaTiO3 nanoparticle/polyvinylbutyral composites
mechanisms.INPUT: Barium titanate (BaTiO3) nanoparticles, polyvinyl butyral (PVB), ethanol, with mixture ratios of 5 wt% (RAM1), 10 wt% (RAM2), and 15 wt% (RAM3) BaTiO3
mechanisms.PROCESS: ultrasonic probe sonication at 20 kHz and 70% amplitude for about 2 h, followed by investigation based on transmission line theory in the frequency range from 1 GHz to 14 GHz
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: BaTiO3 nanoparticles dispersed well in the mixture of PVB/ethanol under probe sonication
mechanisms.OUTPUT: BaTiO3 nanoparticle-PVB composites with different weight concentrations of BaTiO3
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: minimum reflection loss (RL) of RAM1 reaches −3.47 dB in the frequency range 1–14 GHz
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: sonication at 20 kHz, 70% amplitude, about 2 h; microwave measurement frequency range 1–14 GHz
mechanisms.CONTROL: comparison of composites with different BaTiO3 weight concentrations: 5 wt% (RAM1), 10 wt% (RAM2), 15 wt% (RAM3)

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Synthesize and characterize nanometer-sized AlGaN embedded in a poly-methylmethacrylate (PMMA) matrix for potential tunable optoelectronic devices
mechanisms.INPUT: UNKNOWN
mechanisms.PROCESS: UNKNOWN
mechanisms.OUTPUT: AlGaN nanoparticle/polymer composite with defect-free zinc blende AlGaN nanoparticles embedded in PMMA
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Efficient emission in the violet-blue region; formation of defect-free zinc blende AlGaN nanoparticles

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Synthesis of melanin-gold nanoparticle composite material with tunable optical properties using engineered cells.
mechanisms.INPUT: Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) and melanin, produced by engineered bacterial cells.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Bacterial synthesis combining melanin and gold nanoparticles to form a composite material.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Melanin-gold nanoparticle composite material with tunable optical properties.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Optical and electromagnetic properties of gold nanoparticles modulated by melanin; broad absorption spectrum of melanin.
mechanisms.CONSTRAINTS: Complexity of composite material synthesis; need for simple design rules.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Synthesize natural magnetic particles/chitosan/gold nanoparticles composites (NMP/Chi/AuNPs) using a green method.
mechanisms.INPUT: Natural magnetic particles/chitosan (NMP/Chi) and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) synthesized using chitosan as a reducing agent and stabilizer.
mechanisms.PROCESS: AuNPs were synthesized using chitosan as a reducing agent and stabilizer in one step, then AuNPs were impregnated on NMP/Chi at room temperature.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: AuNPs were characterized as spherical with an average of 14.9 nm and absorbed at visible light (~530 nm).
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Natural magnetic particles/chitosan/gold nanoparticles composites (NMP/Chi/AuNPs).
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: In IR spectra, NMP/Chi/AuNP showed a decrease in intensity and peak shift to 1395 cm⁻¹ (stretching vibration of C-O from primary alcohol group) and Fe-O vibrations from Fe₃O₄ shifted from 566 to 583 cm⁻¹.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Develop a nano-sized TiO2-reinforced electroless nickel-based ternary (Ni-W-P) alloy and composite coating on API X60 steel to protect against wear and corrosion.
mechanisms.INPUT: API X60 steel (high-strength carbon steel pipe grade) and an alkaline hypophosphite-reduced bath containing Ni-W-P with TiO2 nanoparticles.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Electroless deposition using an alkaline hypophosphite-reduced bath to form a Ni-W-P/TiO2 composite coating.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: TiO2 nanoparticle-reinforced electroless Ni-W-P composite coating on API X60 steel with a consistent thickness of approximately 24 µm.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Tribological performance evaluated via Vickers microhardness measurements and reciprocating wear tests under dry conditions at a 5 N load; also surface morphology, microstructure, elemental composition, structure, phase evolution, adhesion, and roughness.
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: Electroless deposition from an alkaline hypophosphite-reduced bath; wear tests conducted under dry conditions at a 5 N load.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Synthesis of graphene oxide-silicon nanoparticle (GO-Si NP) composite as potential anode material for lithium ion batteries
mechanisms.INPUT: Graphene oxide and silicon nanoparticles in aqueous solution
mechanisms.PROCESS: Simple method of preparation in aqueous solution
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Graphene oxide-silicon nanoparticle (GO-Si NP) nanocomposite
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Expected improvement in cycling stability of Si NP as an anode material
mechanisms.CONTROL: Composites with various percentage of Si NP

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Fabricating hierarchical nanostructures by surface-confined synthesis of silver nanoparticles on electrospun polyimide nanofibers.
mechanisms.INPUT: Electrospun polyimide nanofibers.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Surface-confined imide cleavage via immersion in aqueous KOH solution, then ion-exchange via immersion in aqueous AgNO3 solution, then reduction (chemical or thermal) of silver ions.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Potassium polyamate coatings of accurately defined thickness formed at a rate of 25 nm h−1; silver ions introduced into polyamate resin.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Composite coating of silver nanoparticles on polyimide nanofibers; via thermal reduction, monodisperse silver nanoparticles (average diameter 5.2 nm) embedded in a re-imidized polyimide surface layer.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Distinct morphologies of nanoparticle coatings depending on reduction mode; nanoparticle size (5.2 nm average diameter for thermal reduction).
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: Aqueous KOH solution immersion, aqueous AgNO3 solution immersion, chemical or thermal reduction.
mechanisms.CONTROL: Comparison of chemical and thermal reduction modes.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: To synthesize a silver nanoparticle composite using a filamentous fungus as a soft bio-template and characterize its structure and functional application in dye degradation.
mechanisms.INPUT: Filamentous fungus (Sclerotium rolfsii) as a soft bio-template and silver nanoparticles (AgNPs).
mechanisms.PROCESS: Self-assembly of silver nanoparticles on the living fungal hyphae bio-template to form microtubules adhering to the hyphae.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Formation of 3D fungal hyphae–silver nanoparticle (FH-AgNP) composite microtubules.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Fungal hyphae–silver nanoparticle (FH-AgNP) composite.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Dye degradation of methylene blue under visible light.
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: Visible light irradiation for dye degradation.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: synthesis of colloidal nanoparticles having well-ordered structures in high yield, environmentally friendly methods and low cost
mechanisms.INPUT: UNKNOWN
mechanisms.PROCESS: chemical reduction using amino acids, peptides and peptide mimetics as reducing agents, with non-covalent interactions (hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic, π-stacking, van der Waals) playing a role
mechanisms.OUTPUT: colloidal nanoparticles as stable, colloidal dispersions in solution
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: UNKNOWN

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Nonlinear inter-modality registration is often challenging due to the lack of objective functions that are good proxies for alignment; propose a synthesis-by-registration method to convert this problem into an easier intra-modality task.
mechanisms.INPUT: Paired images from different modalities (e.g., histological sections and MRI slices)
mechanisms.PROCESS: Synthesis-by-registration method using a registration loss for weakly supervised image translation between domains, driven by a registration U-Net with frozen weights to drive a synthesis CNN, complemented with a structure preserving constraint based on contrastive learning.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Synthesized image from one modality to the other, enabling intra-modality registration
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Registered images (e.g., histological sections registered to MRI slices)
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: 13% reduction in landmark error over mutual information-based registration; 11% reduction over CycleGAN-based synthesis
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: Weakly supervised setting without perfectly aligned training data
mechanisms.CONSTRAINTS: Structure preserving constraint based on contrastive learning prevents blurring and content shifts due to overfitting
mechanisms.CONTROL: Registration based on mutual information and synthesis-based algorithms such as CycleGAN

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Synthesis of titanium-oxide nanoparticles with independent control over size and stoichiometry
mechanisms.INPUT: Ti-O nanoparticles synthesized via hollow cathode sputtering in an Ar-O2 atmosphere using high power pulsing
mechanisms.PROCESS: Hollow cathode sputtering in an Ar-O2 atmosphere using high power pulsing, with independent control of O2 gas flow for stoichiometry and biasing of two separate anodes in the growth zone for size
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Titanium-oxide nanoparticles with diameters in the range of 25 to 75 nm, and with different Ti-O compositions and crystalline phases
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Nanoparticle size and stoichiometry varied independently
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: Ar-O2 atmosphere, high power pulsing, controlled O2 gas flow, independent biasing of two separate anodes in the growth zone

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Explore the use of nanoparticles of gamma Fe2O3 for hyperthermia treatment of living organisms by absorption of 1064 nm radiations from Nd:YAG laser
mechanisms.INPUT: Escherichia coli cells as model system, nanoparticles of gamma Fe2O3 synthesized by DC arc plasma assisted gas phase condensation, lysine as interface
mechanisms.PROCESS: Attachment of nanoparticles of iron oxide along with lysine to cell walls, then absorption of 1064 nm radiations from Nd:YAG laser
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Hyperthermia effect in E. coli cells
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Growth rate measurements and protein assessment of the cells

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Develop a new model for the electron emission of high-Z nanoparticle irradiated by X-rays, motivated by nanoparticle enhancement of cancer treatment by radiotherapy
mechanisms.INPUT: High-Z nanoparticle irradiated by X-rays
mechanisms.PROCESS: Combination of a pure probabilistic analytical model for photon trajectories inside the nanoparticle and subsequent Monte-Carlo simulation of electron cascade trajectories using the Livermore model in Geant4
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Photon absorption and electron cascade production depth in the nanoparticle
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Electron emission from the nanoparticle
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Existence of a nanoparticle optimal radius corresponding to a maximum of nanoparticle electron emission
mechanisms.CONTROL: Comparison of nanoparticle and plane surface electron emissions using a model developed for a plane surface

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Investigate how text-to-speech synthesis techniques can be used for piano MIDI-to-audio synthesis tasks.
mechanisms.INPUT: piano MIDI symbolic input
mechanisms.PROCESS: Applying TTS components (Tacotron and neural source-filter waveform models) to convert MIDI to audio, with minor modifications
mechanisms.OUTPUT: synthesized piano audio
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: subjective quality of synthesized piano audio
mechanisms.CONSTRAINTS: conversion from MIDI to acoustic features is challenging, limiting overall system performance
mechanisms.CONTROL: reference systems using sample-based and physical-modeling-based sound modeling techniques

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: To construct a dataset of codified gold nanoparticle synthesis protocols and outcomes to facilitate data-driven understanding of the underlying mechanisms controlling size and shape.
mechanisms.INPUT: Gold nanoparticle synthesis protocols and outcomes extracted from the nanoparticle materials science literature using natural language processing and text-mining techniques.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Natural language processing and text-mining techniques applied to extract and codify synthesis protocols and outcomes.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: A publicly available dataset containing 5,154 data records, each representing a single gold nanoparticle synthesis.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: UNKNOWN

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Investigate electronic emission of gold nanoparticles (GNPs) under X-ray irradiation and compare to gold bulk electron emission, in the context of using GNPs as a radiotherapy enhancer.
mechanisms.INPUT: Gold Nanoparticles (GNPs) and gold bulk subjected to X-ray irradiation.
mechanisms.PROCESS: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) experiments and simulations using Geant4 toolkit (Livermore and PENELOPE models) for particle transport.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Electronic emission from GNPs after X-ray irradiation, affected by the GNP coating.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Method to determine the coating surface density of GNPs.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Electronic emission spectra (XPS spectra) of GNPs compared to gold bulk.
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: X-ray irradiation, simulation with Geant4 Livermore and PENELOPE models.
mechanisms.CONSTRAINTS: Limitations of the PENELOPE model; coating surface density must be precisely determined.
mechanisms.FAILURE_MODE: Incorrect interpretation of GNP electronic emission without accounting for coating.
mechanisms.CONTROL: Gold bulk electron emission (comparison with GNP emission).

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Prediction of nonlinear micro/meso-mechanical response of the fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites, considering two dominant damage mechanisms: matrix elasto-plastic response and fibre-matrix decohesion
mechanisms.INPUT: Fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) composite microstructure represented by a representative volume element (RVE) with matrix, fibres (modelled as linear-elastic transversely isotropic), and cohesive interfaces
mechanisms.PROCESS: Three-dimensional multi-scale computational homogenisation framework implemented within hierarchic finite element, using a non-associative pressure dependent paraboloidal yield criterion for matrix, cohesive interface elements for decohesion, and a unified approach to impose RVE boundary conditions (linear displacement, uniform traction, or periodic)
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Matrix elasto-plastic deformation and fibre-matrix decohesion (damage mechanisms)
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Nonlinear micro/meso-mechanical response of the FRP composite
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Nonlinear micro/meso-mechanical response including damage initiation and evolution
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: RVE boundary conditions can be linear displacement, uniform traction, or periodic; arbitrary orders of approximation can be used

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: To develop a novel synthesis for near monodisperse, sub-10-nm Bi2Te3 nanoparticles and characterize their thermoelectric properties.
mechanisms.INPUT: Bismuth nanoparticles obtained via a new reduction route.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Formation of rhombohedral Bi2Te3 nanoparticles from bismuth nanoparticles, followed by ligand removal using hydrazine hydrate etching, and spark plasma sintering into a pellet.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Near monodisperse, sub-10-nm Bi2Te3 nanoparticles with ligands attached, then ligand-free nanoparticles.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: A sintered pellet of Bi2Te3 nanoparticles with preserved crystal grain sizes.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Highly reduced thermal conductivity and same electric conductivity as bulk n-type Bi2Te3.
mechanisms.CONSTRAINTS: Near monodisperse, sub-10-nm particle size; rhombohedral crystal structure.
mechanisms.CONTROL: Bulk n-type Bi2Te3 as comparison for thermoelectric properties.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: To compute composite spectra using different galaxy evolution models and SSP libraries with ease and efficiency, enabling the interpretation of the integrated light of galaxies and stellar clusters.
mechanisms.INPUT: Empirical and/or theoretical libraries of the spectral energy distribution emitted by simple stellar populations (SSPs) and models of the star formation history (SFH) and chemical evolution.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Stellar population synthesis combining SSP libraries with SFH and chemical evolution models, incorporating cosmic redshift and dust extinction.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Composite spectra computed from the combination of SSPs, SFH, and chemical evolution models.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Composite spectra and several observable quantities derived from the spectra, including broadband photometric fluxes.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Estimation of essential galaxy properties such as total stellar mass, star formation rate, mass-weighted age and metallicity.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Discuss the quantum mechanics of many-body systems in hybrid microgels consisting of negatively charged anionic microgels with a thick sheath of water molecules and a nanoparticle captivated within.
mechanisms.INPUT: Negatively charged anionic microgels with protruding anionic moieties solvated by a thick sheath of water molecules, and a nanoparticle captivated within the microgel.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Synthesis of a nanoparticle within the microgel, where the thermodynamic feasibility depends on the magnitude of interaction between nanoparticle, water molecules, and microgel relative to the sum of self-interaction between counterions and interaction between counterions and microgel.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Nanoparticle with a thick electronic cloud that oscillates under the influence of the net interaction potential of charged anionic moieties and solvent water molecules.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: A hybrid microgel system with a synthesized nanoparticle having an oscillating electronic cloud.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: The Hamiltonian describing the energy of the oscillating electronic cloud wrapped around the nanoparticle, derived as the product of the integral of electron density and its position vector over all space multiplied with the net electric potential.
mechanisms.CONSTRAINTS: Thermodynamic feasibility depends on the relative magnitudes of interactions as described.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Achieving both realism and diversity in industrial anomaly synthesis, breaking the diversity-realism trade-off dilemma
mechanisms.INPUT: Normal images of industrial objects
mechanisms.PROCESS: Synergizing Vision Language Large Model (VLLM), Latent Diffusion Model (LDM), and texture library Tex-9K; VLLM generates reasonable anomaly text descriptions for each industrial object, matched with diverse textures from Tex-9K; textures guide LDM via ControlNet to paint on normal images; Texture-Aware Latent Init stabilizes the natural-image-trained ControlNet for industrial images
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Anomaly text descriptions generated by VLLM and matched with relevant textures from Tex-9K
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Realistic and diverse industrial anomaly images
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Outperforms existing methods in realism and diversity

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: extend traditional (vocoder-based) DNN-TTS with articulatory input, estimated from ultrasound tongue images, to improve naturalness of synthesized speech in limited-data scenarios
mechanisms.INPUT: text and ultrasound tongue image-based articulatory input
mechanisms.PROCESS: DNN-based text-to-speech synthesis with articulatory input from ultrasound tongue images
mechanisms.OUTPUT: synthesized speech
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: naturalness of synthesized speech
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: limited-data scenarios, data from eight speakers

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: control over the size and shape of colloidal silver nanoparticles via photo-induced synthesis and light-driven nanoengineering
mechanisms.INPUT: UNKNOWN
mechanisms.PROCESS: photo-induced synthesis by varying the amount and type of the stabilizing agent and the type of optical irradiation
mechanisms.OUTPUT: colloidal silver nanoparticles with manipulated sizes and shapes
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: UNKNOWN
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: varying the amount and type of the stabilizing agent and the type of optical irradiation

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Manage jointly the energy demand of a large group of consumers or users for charging electric vehicle batteries, to tackle the heterogenous scenario of aggregators and individual consumers using composite games.
mechanisms.INPUT: Networks of electric vehicles with aggregators and individual consumers, each requiring charging an EV battery.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Exploiting the notion of composite game and equilibrium for the first time in smart grid literature to model the distributed charging problem.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Formation of coalitions where an aggregator manages joint demand of a group of users, leading to a distributed charging policy.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Equilibrium charging policy resulting from the composite game, affecting network costs.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Impact on distribution network costs, specifically Joule losses and transformer ageing.
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: Smart grids encompassing distributed electrical networks with simultaneous presence of aggregators and individual consumers.
mechanisms.CONSTRAINTS: Charging policy is chosen by users or aggregators, implying distributed decision-making and potential user preferences.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: synthesis of planar antenna arrays by optimizing phase excitation coefficients to best meet a desired radiation pattern
mechanisms.INPUT: planar antenna arrays with rectangular cells using a probe feed, and phase excitation coefficients
mechanisms.PROCESS: fuzzy genetic algorithms (FGAs) that adjust control parameters of a standard genetic algorithm using a fuzzy controller based on the best individual fitness and the population diversity measurements
mechanisms.OUTPUT: desired radiation pattern and optimized phase excitation coefficients
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: good agreement between the desired and calculated radiation patterns, and superior capabilities with respect to the standard version (SGAs)

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: To overcome the need for pairwise aligned MR and CT training images and avoid errors from misalignment in MR-to-CT synthesis for MR-only radiotherapy treatment planning.
mechanisms.INPUT: Unpaired 2D brain MR image slices (and CT images for cycle consistency) from 24 patients.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Training a generative adversarial network (GAN) with two synthesis CNNs and two discriminator CNNs using cycle consistency to transform 2D brain MR image slices into 2D brain CT image slices and vice versa.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Synthesized CT images that closely approximate reference CT images.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Quantitative evaluation showing synthesized CT images closely approximate reference CT images and outperform a GAN model trained with paired MR and CT images.
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: Training with cycle consistency on 2D brain MR and CT slices from 24 patients.
mechanisms.CONSTRAINTS: Current methods require pairwise aligned MR and CT training images of the same patient; misalignment between paired images can lead to errors.
mechanisms.CONTROL: A GAN model trained with paired MR and CT images.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Study the effect of electric field on the photoluminescence (PL) from a composite of conjugated polymer mixed with zinc oxide nanoparticles.
mechanisms.INPUT: A composite film consisting of a conjugated polymer mixed with zinc oxide nanoparticles.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Application of a voltage bias to planar gold electrodes.
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: Suppression of green-yellow emission and shift of the PL emission maximum towards the blue region; generation of excited states including formation of polymer-nanoparticle complexes, exciplex states, and charge transfer between polymer and nanoparticle.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Photoluminescence emission: in absence of electric field, two maxima in blue and green-yellow regions; under electric field, a single maximum in the blue region.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Photoluminescence emission spectra and current-voltage characteristics exhibiting non-linear behavior typical of non-homogeneous polymer-inorganic structures.
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: Application of voltage bias to planar gold electrodes; specific field strength, temperature, and environment not stated.
mechanisms.CONTROL: PL emission in the absence of electric field (no voltage bias).

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: To analyze and compare opinions of a large number of text-to-speech and voice conversion systems from past challenges, determine whether and how opinions change over time, and collect a large-scale dataset of synthetic samples and ratings for further research.
mechanisms.INPUT: Publicly-available system samples and listening test results from Blizzard Challenge and Voice Conversion Challenge.
mechanisms.PROCESS: Conducting a large-scale listening test with samples from many challenges combined.
mechanisms.OUTPUT: A large-scale dataset of a diverse variety of synthetic samples and their ratings.
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Strong correlations challenge by challenge at the system level.

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: Evaluate in a microscopic theory the shear modulus and the magnetophonon and magnetoplasmon dispersions of the composite fermion Wigner crystal, and determine the region of stability of the crystal phase and relate the frequency of its pinning mode to that of the corresponding electron crystal near integer fillings.
mechanisms.INPUT: Composite fermion Wigner crystal in the vicinity of filling factors 1/3, 2/5, and 3/7
mechanisms.PROCESS: Microscopic theory calculation of shear modulus and magnetophonon and magnetoplasmon dispersions
mechanisms.OUTPUT: Region of stability of the crystal phase and relationship between the pinning mode frequency of the composite fermion Wigner crystal and that of the corresponding electron crystal near integer fillings
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: Good semiquantitative agreement with experiment, supporting the identification of the optical resonance as the pinning mode of the composite fermions Wigner crystal
mechanisms.CONTROL: Corresponding electron crystal near integer fillings

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: to restrict, by means of priorities, the set of possible interactions in such a way as to guarantee the given safety conditions for all possible runs
mechanisms.INPUT: a set of interacting components with non-deterministic variable update and given safety requirements, and a communication architecture specifying possible communication paths between local controllers
mechanisms.PROCESS: distributed priority synthesis: obtaining local sets of priorities, deployed in terms of local component controllers sharing intended next moves between components in local neighborhoods only, defined as a multi-player safety game between players for selecting next transition and an environment for updating uncontrollable variables
mechanisms.OUTPUT: local sets of priorities that guarantee the safety conditions
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: UNKNOWN
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: communication architecture specifying possible communication paths between local controllers; local neighborhoods for sharing intended next moves
mechanisms.CONSTRAINTS: communication architecture limits which components can share information; environment demonically updates uncontrollable variables

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: provides students with a hands-on experience in nanomaterials chemistry and characterization
mechanisms.INPUT: UNKNOWN
mechanisms.PROCESS: use air-free chemistry procedures to synthesize and separate iron oxide magnetic nanoparticles and subsequently modify the nanoparticle surface using a chemical stripping agent; characterized using electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering, and magnetophotometer
mechanisms.OUTPUT: superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles with modified surface
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: magnetic characterization using an open-source (3D-printed), inexpensive magnetophotometer; morphology and chemical composition via electron microscopy and dynamic light scattering

mechanisms.OBJECTIVE: to explore and design nanoparticles composites with specific optical properties, specifically to achieve a tunable absorber film
mechanisms.INPUT: a composite material comprising periodically distributed metallic spheres in a dielectric host matrix
mechanisms.PROCESS: effective non-retarded method (ENR) to obtain the effective macroscopic dielectric function and calculate the electromagnetic response of a slab
mechanisms.INTERMEDIATE_STATE: effective macroscopic dielectric function and its resonance frequencies
mechanisms.OUTPUT: tunable absorber film
mechanisms.MEASURED_EFFECT: optical properties for different filling fractions, especially in the vicinity of resonance frequencies; electromagnetic response compared with that from the Korringa-Kohn-Rostoker (KKR) method
mechanisms.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: different filling fractions of metallic spheres; in the vicinity of resonance frequencies of the macroscopic dielectric function
